function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single individual—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed and studied for millennia. Ancient Greeks noted static electricity from amber, while modern scientific understanding began to take shape in the 17th‑18th centuries with figures such as William Gilbert (who coined the term “electricus”), Benjamin Franklin (his kite experiment), and later Alessandro Volta (inventor of the voltaic pile). Subsequent work by scientists like Michael Faraday and James Clerk Maxwell built the foundation for our contemporary knowledge of electromagnetism.
